Skellam Regression

Source: R/skellam.reg.R
skellam.reg.Rd

Fits a regression model in which a difference of counts \(y = Y_1 - Y_2\) follows a Skellam distribution and both rates depend on covariates through log links.

Usage

skellam.reg(formula, data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

formula

A formula y ~ x1 + x2 (the same covariates for both rates) or a two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2, where the part before | is the model for \(\lambda_1\) and the part after it the model for \(\lambda_2\). Offsets can be given with offset() in either part. For the original interface, a numeric vector y; see Details.

data

A data frame containing the variables in the formula. For the original interface, the covariates x.

...

For the original interface, y and x may also be given by name.

Value

An object of class "skellam_reg", a list with components

coefficients

A list with the coefficient vectors lambda1 and lambda2.

vcov

Covariance matrix of all coefficients.

loglik

Maximised log-likelihood.

param1, param2

Coefficient tables (estimate, standard error, Wald statistic, p-value) for \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\), as returned by earlier versions.

fitted.values

A data frame with the fitted rates lambda1 and lambda2.

y, nobs, df.residual, converged, call, formula, terms, levels

The response used, the number of observations, the residual degrees of freedom, whether the optimizer converged, and what is needed to predict on new data.

Methods are available for print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik (hence AIC, BIC), nobs, confint (the default method), fitted, residuals, predict, simulate, anova and update.

Details

The response is modelled as \(y_i = Y_{1i} - Y_{2i}\) with independent \(Y_{1i} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_{1i})\) and \(Y_{2i} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_{2i})\), and \(\log\lambda_{1i} = x_{1i}^\top\beta_1\), \(\log\lambda_{2i} = x_{2i}^\top\beta_2\). So the lambda1 coefficients describe the rate of the counts that are added and the lambda2 coefficients the rate of the counts that are subtracted, as in dskellam(y, lambda1, lambda2).

The log-likelihood is computed with dskellam(log = TRUE) and maximised by optim (BFGS) with the analytic gradient, from deterministic starting values (least-squares fits of the log moment estimates of an intercept-only model), so repeated calls give identical results. Standard errors come from the inverse of the observed information (optimHess). Observations with missing values in any variable used are removed with a warning. A warning is also given if the optimizer does not converge or the information matrix is not invertible (standard errors are then NA).

Original interface. skellam.reg(y, x) with a numeric response y and a vector, matrix or data frame of covariates x fits the model with the same covariates (and an intercept) for both rates, exactly as in earlier versions of the package.

References

  • Skellam, J. G. (1946) The frequency distribution of the difference between two Poisson variates belonging to different populations. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A 109(3), 296.

  • Karlis, D. and Ntzoufras, I. (2009) Bayesian modelling of football outcomes: using the Skellam's distribution for the goal difference. IMA Journal of Management Mathematics 20(2), 133-145.

See also

predict.skellam_reg, skellam.fit for a single sample, skellam for the distribution.

Author

Michail Tsagris; formula interface and methods by Montasser Ghachem and Oguz Ersan

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(attack = rnorm(n), defence = rnorm(n))
d$goaldiff <- rpois(n, exp(0.4 + 0.3 * d$attack)) -
              rpois(n, exp(0.1 - 0.2 * d$defence))

# different covariates for the two rates
m <- skellam.reg(goaldiff ~ attack | defence, data = d)
m
#> Skellam regression
#> 
#> Call:
#> skellam.reg(formula = goaldiff ~ attack | defence, data = d)
#> 
#> Coefficients for log(lambda1), the rate of the counts that are added:
#> (Intercept)      attack 
#>      0.4848      0.2097 
#> 
#> Coefficients for log(lambda2), the rate of the counts that are subtracted:
#> (Intercept)     defence 
#>     0.22359    -0.07533 
#> 
#> n = 500, log-likelihood -974.2896, AIC 1956.579
summary(m)
#> 
#> Call:
#> skellam.reg(formula = goaldiff ~ attack | defence, data = d)
#> 
#> log(lambda1): rate of the counts that are added
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  0.48485    0.06562   7.389 1.48e-13 ***
#> attack       0.20972    0.04320   4.855 1.20e-06 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> log(lambda2): rate of the counts that are subtracted
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
#> (Intercept)  0.22359    0.08114   2.755  0.00586 **
#> defence     -0.07533    0.05224  -1.442  0.14926   
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> n = 500, residual df = 496, log-likelihood -974.2896, AIC 1956.579, BIC 1973.438

# nested models: likelihood-ratio test
m0 <- skellam.reg(goaldiff ~ 1 | 1, data = d)
anova(m0, m)
#> Likelihood ratio test
#> 
#> Model 1: goaldiff ~ 1 | 1
#> Model 2: goaldiff ~ attack | defence
#> 
#>         #Df  LogLik Df  Chisq Pr(>Chisq)    
#> Model 1   2 -987.07                         
#> Model 2   4 -974.29  2 25.564  2.811e-06 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

# probabilities of each goal difference for new data
predict(m, newdata = data.frame(attack = 1, defence = 0), type = "prob", at = -2:2)
#>             -2        -1         0         1         2
#> [1,] 0.0648087 0.1400983 0.2158241 0.2243766 0.1662352

# original interface: same covariates (and an intercept) for both rates
skellam.reg(d$goaldiff, d$attack)$param1
#>              Estimate Std. Error Wald value      p-value
#> (Intercept) 0.4854379 0.06578229   7.379462 1.589310e-13
#> x           0.2097604 0.06084470   3.447472 5.658591e-04
